scenarios.name: Separate brief alternating voices from actual audio
scenarios.given: a 20-second on-device recording contains two known distinct synthetic voices with short and long alternating turns
scenarios.when: the production diarizer analyzes the audio and its timeline is applied to the transcript
scenarios.then: each known voice retains one label, the two voices have different labels, and no expected turn is merged into the other person

manual.reason: Native Mac CoreML inference establishes model behavior on these fixtures; it does not establish the original private recording or physical iPhone speed and accuracy.
steps: Compare the reported recording locally if the maintainer shares its retained audio.
Exercise speaker labels on physical iPhone with different people and record source, accuracy and performance separately.

scenarios.name: Keep one voice together across pauses
scenarios.given: a recording contains one known voice speaking sentences of different lengths with pauses
scenarios.when: the actual on-device diarizer labels the timed transcript
scenarios.then: the known turns retain one speaker identity rather than becoming invented extra speakers

scenarios.name: Separate held-out voices without tuning to one pair
scenarios.given: a second pair of known stock voices alternates in a short imbalanced recording not used in the initial diagnosis
scenarios.when: the production model labels the timed turns
scenarios.then: the two people have different labels and each returning voice retains its label

scenarios.name: Keep returning voices distinct through the full dialogue
scenarios.given: two known voices alternate eight times with unequal sentence lengths and brief replies
scenarios.when: the complete recording is analyzed by the actual production model
scenarios.then: every known turn maps to its own person with one stable identity per voice

scenarios.name: Construct the device speaker model without downloading or backing up its assets
scenarios.given: speaker identification has not been prepared and the model cache is present or missing
scenarios.when: the production device diarizer is constructed
scenarios.then: its actual cache is excluded from backups and no model asset is downloaded until preparation is explicitly requested

scenarios.name: Keep returning voices through silence in the same recording
scenarios.given: two real known voices are labeled and one renamed in an active recording
scenarios.when: streaming analysis continues through silence and a later window with no earlier shared audio
scenarios.then: the same recording retains both voice identities and the edited name; a different stream epoch cannot inherit them

scenarios.name: Release prediction state when the recording ends
scenarios.given: an active recording owns real model prediction state
scenarios.when: that recording ends or is cancelled and model work drains
scenarios.then: the worker retains no probability history or voice state from the ended recording, and a late cleanup cannot reset a newer recording

scenarios.name: Stop flushes the delayed speaker tail
scenarios.given: the streaming model has delayed words and no new microphone samples have arrived since its last pass
scenarios.then: one final live flush labels the last words and closes that run without routing through file analysis

scenarios.name: Turning speaker identification off releases the active voice state
scenarios.given: speaker inference is pending during a microphone recording
scenarios.then: the speaker buffer and run are released immediately and late model results cannot label the transcript while recording remains independently stoppable

scenarios.name: Delayed model output replaces only confirmed audio
scenarios.given: the transcript already has speaker labels beyond the streaming models confirmed time
scenarios.when: a partial result or confirmed silence updates an earlier interval
scenarios.then: labels beyond the confirmed horizon survive, only confirmed silence clears prior labels, and no segment claims unseen or flush-padding audio

scenarios.name: Overlapping live windows and Stop preserve voice identities
scenarios.given: one recording contains known alternating voices and several live windows share the same audio
scenarios.when: periodic analysis repeats and grows those windows before Stop flushes the decoder
scenarios.then: audio is fed once, every known turn keeps its speaker, flush padding claims no captured time and repeated Stop preserves the completed result

scenarios.name: A lost audio gap or new recording cannot inherit an old voice identity
scenarios.given: a live recording has identified two voices
scenarios.when: unheard audio creates a gap or a new recording starts and old cleanup arrives late
scenarios.then: a new epoch separates the identities, stale recording requests are rejected, and old cleanup does not reset the new recording

scenarios.name: Long recordings bound prediction history while retaining voice identity
scenarios.given: a real model has heard two known voices in one recording
scenarios.when: the recording continues beyond ten minutes and those voices return
scenarios.then: at most ten minutes of prediction probabilities remain, absolute time and identities remain stable, and ending the run releases its prediction history

scenarios.name: File imports require foreground preparation and remain separate from live analysis
scenarios.given: live and file speaker models require preparation and the file assets fail to load
scenarios.when: an import arrives before preparation, the user retries preparation and then imports during a live recording
scenarios.then: the import starts no preparation, partial failure remains unavailable until Retry, and prepared file analysis cannot change the live voice state

scenarios.name: Cancelled preparation cannot publish labels or poison the next recording
scenarios.given: speaker preparation is pending for a live recording
scenarios.when: that work is cancelled and the recording ends before another recording starts
scenarios.then: the ended run retains no predictions or labels and the new recording identifies the known voices despite late old cleanup
